title: Canada participates in G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee
excerpt: Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu met with international counterparts to discuss global trade priorities and supply chain resilience.
bodyHtml:
The Government of Canada announced on October 2, 2026, that the Honourable Maninder Sidhu, Minister of International Trade, concluded his participation in the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting held in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

During the event, the Minister engaged in discussions regarding the global trading system, including the weaponization of food through coercive trade actions, the eradication of forced labour from global supply chains, and structural excess capacity and production. Minister Sidhu also participated in discussions regarding the most-favored nation principle.

Minister Sidhu held meetings with various international counterparts, including representatives from India, France, the European Union, Saudi Arabia, Poland, Türkiye, Australia, Brazil, the United States, Mexico, China, Germany, Japan, and Indonesia. Additionally, Canada participated in the Global Forum on Steel Excess Capacity ministerial meeting to address steel excess capacity and protect jobs.

The Minister also conducted a Wisconsin business program to promote Canada-United States cross-border trade and investment. The G20 Leaders’ Summit is scheduled to take place in Miami, Florida, in December.
